newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end mixed, off peaks.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end mixed, off peaks.

text.p: April 11 - IMM currency futures ended moderate-volume trading mixed, off peaks. Brokers tied gains in Swiss franc partly to safe-haven buying linked to big losses in U.S. bonds, stocks on ideas U.S. rates will go higher. Shortcovering also aided other units before the weekend on intervention jitters, although some looked for more currency downside next week. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
March U.S. producer prices slipped 0.1 percent and rose 0.4 percent without food and energy. Economists had expected overall PPI to remain flat, with a 0.1-percent core rate rise.
Retail sales rose 0.2 percent vs 0.6-percent rise expected. Without autos, sales rose 0.5 percent compared to a 0.4-percent gain forecast. February's and January's gains were revised sharply upward.

Brokers said the core PPI and the revised prior-month retail sales figures pressured U.S. credit and equity markets most by suggesting the Federal Reserve has plenty of reason to raise rates again to guard against any uptick in inflation.
They waited to see whether Tuesday's U.S. consumer price index cements that sentiment.

In a morning speech, Federal Reserve vice chairman Alice Rivlin said wages are beginning to move up across the board but not rapidly and added that there is no danger of the U.S. economy running out of steam.
Many brokers viewed currencies as still vulnerable on the downside, given the view that U.S. rates are headed higher.
But currency players stayed more on edge about the possibility of central bank intervention to brake the dollar's recent rally, especially against the yen.
"It's (currency market) going to the downside," said a floor broker. "But I don't think anybody wants to take anything home over the weekend."

Japan's finance minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said Friday that Japan will take appropriate steps against excessive movements in the foreign exchange market, reinforcing expectations of, and periodic rumors about, BoJ intervention.

The Ministry of Finance also tried to shoot down remarks by cabinet minister Kabun Muto, who said overnight there was nothing wrong with the dollar above 125 yen and that, in terms of purchasing power, 150 dollar/yen would be appropriate.
An MOF official said, however, that Muto's comments do not reflect official Japan policy and that the MoF is concerned about the yen's recent overdone fall.

June yen ended down $0.000015 at $0.008010, marks eased $0.0007 to $0.5838, Swiss francs rose $0.0036 to $0.6890, sterling gained $0.0046 to $1.6268, Canadian dollar fell $0.0028 to $0.7178, Aussie dollar rose $0.0008 to $0.7842, amd Mexican peso slipped $0.000050 to $0.122575.
